correctness.rationale: For every integer n at least three, F_c(z)=sum_i(z_i-mean z)^4-c(sum_i(z_i-mean z)^2)^2 is a symmetric quartic, so Riener Theorem 1.3 reduces both universal inequalities to two-valued vectors. Exact normalization yields \(q(k)=n/[k(n-k)]-3/n\); its extrema give the stated rational m_n and M_n, attained by explicit vectors. To optimize BM over all isomorphisms, feasible positive-definite ellipsoids are characterized by affine constraints and block-matrix positive semidefinite constraints. Their convex feasible set can be averaged under \(S_n\), and an \(S_n\)-invariant quadratic form on the zero-sum space is scalar Euclidean. Therefore d_BM^4=M_n/m_n globally. The embedded checker replays exact algebra and diagnostic numerical cases, not substituting sampling for the universal lemmas.

value.rationale: The standard real zero-sum hyperplane of the classical ell-four space is a natural irreducible \(S_n\)-representation and canonical codimension-one example. The result computes its exact Euclidean Banach--Mazur invariant for every dimension, with explicit attained inequalities, a strict even/odd law, the exceptional Hilbertian \(n=3\) case, and \(n^{1/4}\) sharp asymptotics. These are meaningful all-dimension geometrical distinctions, not merely a single numerical sample or an arbitrary parameter variation.
